title: Recovery from ADHD energy crash
context: Discussing energy depletion cycles, burnout recovery strategies. The pattern: hyperfocus → exhaustion → guilt → forced rest → repeat.

title: You're trying to solve an emotional problem with a depleted nervous system
context: It's like trying to have therapy while running a marathon. You can't do the work until you stop. Rest is not laziness.

title: ADHD and the Interest-Based Nervous System
context: William Dodson — ADHD motivation isn't broken willpower, it's a different reward system entirely. Interest, challenge, novelty, urgency.

title: Naming avoidance and procrastination
context: Trying to develop vocabulary for categorizing tasks being put off. Not all avoidance is the same — fear, boredom, overwhelm, perfectionism.

title: Energy log: woke up at 6, crashed by 10. The pattern is accelerating.
context: Three days in a row. Morning burst followed by complete shutdown. Coffee doesn't help — it's not tiredness, it's depletion.

title: Burnout Is Not Just Exhaustion — It's Depersonalization
context: The three dimensions of burnout: exhaustion, cynicism, and reduced efficacy. I recognize all three.

title: Self-assessment of current challenges
context: Severe energy depletion, avoidance patterns — tension between building and recovery. I want to build but I can't. The guilt is the worst part.

title: ADHD Burnout Recovery: A Non-Linear Process
context: Recovery isn't a straight line — expect setbacks, plan for them. Two steps forward, one step back is still progress.

title: The crash is not the problem. The problem is the acceleration before the crash that I never see coming.
context: I need something that can see the pattern I can't see. An early warning system for my own behavior.

title: Spoon Theory and Chronic Energy Management
context: Finite energy budget — spending spoons wisely. Every decision costs energy. Plan for depletion, not just productivity.

title: Body doubling and accountability structures for ADHD
context: Working alongside someone — even virtually — dramatically reduces task avoidance. The presence of another mind helps.

title: The ADHD Tax: Hidden Costs of Executive Dysfunction
context: Late fees, missed deadlines, impulse purchases, abandoned subscriptions. The financial and emotional cost of a brain that works differently.
